featured_reviews.name: Niyati Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Every single interaction with Discovery events has been an exhausting cycle of delays, excuses, rescheduling, and the creation of endless WhatsApp groups that achieve absolutely nothing. If there were awards for poor coordination, lack of accountability, and wasting people’s time, your team would win unanimously.

What’s most frustrating is not even the delays themselves — it’s the complete absence of professionalism, ownership, communication, and execution. Every task that should have been straightforward somehow turns into a prolonged discussion with no actual outcome. Timelines are never respected, commitments are casually broken, and instead of solutions, we get more messages, more confusion, and yet another group being made.

Honestly, the only thing your team seems exceptionally efficient at is:
1. Rescheduling meetings
2. Saying “we’ll update you shortly”
3. Creating WhatsApp groups
4. Passing responsibility from one person to another

For a wedding planning/decor company, the inability to actually plan or coordinate is genuinely impressive.

A wedding is already stressful enough without having to constantly chase the people who were hired specifically to reduce that stress. Instead, dealing with your team has become a full-time job in itself.

There has been zero sense of urgency, zero proactive communication, and absolutely no confidence that anything will happen unless we personally follow up ten times. At this stage, it feels less like working with professionals and more like managing a disorganized college project team.

Please understand that people are trusting you with important events, significant amounts of money, and once-in-a-lifetime moments. The least your clients deserve is basic competence, respect for timelines, and honest communication.

I sincerely hope you improve your systems because the current experience has been unbelievably disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Bharat Kathpalia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience with Discovery Events, led by Shailesh Gandhi and his son Yash, was deeply disappointing and fell far below the expected standard for professional wedding planning. We encountered a pattern of mismanagement, lack of accountability, and a noticeable absence of leadership.

The coordination between the father-son duo was minimal, leaving us uncertain about who would be present, which was the opposite of the clarity we sought. We were shocked by a complete lack of care or client hand-holding.

Absence and Lack of Onsite Management
- The Discovery team was not visibly present, forcing the family to handle essential wedding planner responsibilities, including vendor coordination, guest logistics, and timeline management.
- There was no senior, qualified individual overseeing the event; execution felt ad hoc, reactive, and poorly coordinated.
- The onsite team primarily consisted of very young staff (around 23–25 years old) with limited experience. Decisions requiring judgment were frequently escalated to the family or the bride and groom, instead of being handled by the planning team.
- The team was even escalating issues like vendor arrival delays and room readiness directly to the bride and groom.

Consistent Communication Failures
- RSVP team often went silent, leading to multiple guest complaints.
- The hospitality team failed to allocate a guest room, and we had to repeatedly correct the guest list ourselves.
- We had to chase the team for updates on stationery, vendor cabs, and timelines, with little to no proactive response or communication from Discovery.
- There was repeated pushback on our ideas (sound/lighting, rickshaw, cocktail décor, etc.), meaning the final execution often did not match the family's vision.

Major Issues During the Wedding
- Rooming information was not communicated on time, forcing the family to assign rooms directly with hotel staff on Day 0.
- Important hotel traditions and customs were never conveyed to us, causing avoidable confusion, despite Discovery’s claim of hosting many weddings at the property.
- Bridal mehndi was poorly scheduled in a dark, dingy room with no alternatives offered.
- The Sangeet entry was mishandled, and the sound check for an external vendor appeared poorly coordinated.
- Photographers were managed by the family, with the team repeatedly discussing timings with the bride and groom instead of a Discovery representative.
- Pooja materials, despite being communicated well in advance, did not arrive on time.

Transparency and Professionalism Concerns
- When elements were arranged independently (bangles, rickshaw, DJ truck, postcards), we noticed a visible decline in Discovery’s involvement and support.
- There was no transparency in the actual cost of elements, raising concerns about markups and unclear pricing.
- A team member's highly unprofessional comment about a deduction coming from their paycheck, following an instruction from Shailesh.

Overall, our experience with Discovery Events did not reflect the professionalism, reliability, or expertise expected of a wedding planning company. We hope the company addresses the significant gaps in their service standards.

featured_reviews.name: Ritika Kapoor
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a really disappointing experience in the eight months leading up to our wedding, and honestly, the wedding days themselves were even worse.

To start with, Yash Gandhi—the person we signed the contract with—basically disappeared just three months into planning. Calls went unanswered, messages were ignored, and communication completely dropped off.

During the planning process, anytime we didn’t agree with their ideas, the response felt dismissive and sometimes even condescending. We were made to feel like our preferences were unreasonable. They initially said they’d help with design and décor, but it became clear they were more comfortable offering generic, template-style setups. When we pushed for something more design-focused, instead of working with us, they kept bringing the conversation back to budget and making us feel bad about it.

They also connected us with a décor designer from their team who spoke to us once, disappeared for almost a month, and then came back asking for an additional fee—despite clearly saying earlier that there wouldn’t be one. That whole experience just felt unprofessional and disorganized.

On the wedding days, things were chaotic. Most of the responsibility fell on a small, junior team who, while trying their best, were clearly overwhelmed. We kept getting interrupted during our own events with basic questions that should have been handled by Yash or Shailesh. Meanwhile, the senior team was mostly absent, Shailesh was mostly in the room, showing up briefly like guests rather than actually running the wedding and Yash didn’t  care to even show up at the wedding

One of the most disappointing moments was around the fireworks—a key element we were really looking forward to as part of our celebration. They were unable to execute it and told us it had to be cancelled due to venue restrictions. We later found out this wasn’t true, and they couldn’t execute a basic thing.

Please go to anyone else but them.
